chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hanan ibn Sadir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Every sin that killing in the way of Allah (Exalted and Mighty) expiates, except for debt; there is no expiation for it except its payment, or the creditor paying it off, or the one who has the right forgiving.

key_terms.الْقَتْلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: Killing in the way of Allah (martyrdom)

ai.seo_question: Does martyrdom erase all sins including financial debts?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies that while martyrdom expiates all sins, financial debts (al-dayn) remain a distinct obligation requiring fulfillment through payment, creditor settlement, or forgiveness. This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly view that debts are rights of the people (huquq al-nas) and thus persist beyond the spiritual purification of martyrdom, unlike sins against God. The narration highlights the necessity of settling one's financial dues before the final accounting, emphasizing the continuity of earthly obligations in the afterlife.
